transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-09 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~30 mins | Attendees: Maya, Liam (Redwood) - Priya, Jon, Sara (NexaHealth)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, uh quick check in today, we wanted to cover onboarding progress, network, and the baseline runs.
[00:18] Priya Kapoor: thanks Maya, yep we've got Priya here, small heads up we did upload a sample dataset to the shared bucket, but we still need to get service account permissions worked out.
[00:28] Jon Martinez: yeah I'm on the VPC side, peering started but had a couple things with egress rules — corporate firewall is blocking some of the outbound ranges, so I need the exact CIDR and ports from you.
[00:42] Liam O'Connor: ok Jon, we can provide the peering CIDR list; it's the typical, um, redwood dedicated endpoints and the control plane, sorry sometimes the auto-transcriber calls it Redwood Dedicate, but it's Redwood Dedicated endpoints on 10.4.0.0/16 and 10.5.0.0/16 for the pool. We'll send exact ranges after the call.
[01:05] Sara Lee: from security, we're mostly concerned about KMS integration and audit logs retention — we need to know if keys are customer-managed and how long logs are kept. Also SOC2 artefacts you mentioned last week?
[01:20] Maya Chen: yeah great question. Keys can be customer-managed via KMS/HSM on the private deployment; for hosted pilots we typically support customer KMS through our hybrid keyflow — I'll send the KMS integration doc. Audit logs are retained 90 days by default for the pilot but we can extend that in Dedicated/Private plans. We'll attach SOC2 summary doc as well.
[01:42] Priya Kapoor: perfect, can you also confirm data residency? Our legal team wants to ensure data stays in us-west-2.
[01:49] Maya Chen: yes, for this pilot we've pinned region to us-west-2, and the storage buckets are in that region. If you move to Private we can do on-prem or VPC-only models.
[02:02] Jon Martinez: for the peering, I need a precise list of IPs and a sample iptables entry. Also what about NAT and egress, will Redwood call out to external token exchanges?
[02:14] Liam O'Connor: good point — control plane calls go over the peered connection; outbound to public model registries only happens if you enable model fetching from outside. For the pilot we'll use the pre-bundled open model so no external calls. I'll send the iptables snippet.
[02:31] Priya Kapoor: sounds good. On the performance side, we ran a small internal test against their existing self-hosted instance — median latency was about 220ms per token which is too high for our product goal. We're hoping Redwood can show lower p99s on the dedicated nodes.
[02:48] Liam O'Connor: understood. We'll run a baseline benchmark on a comparable sequence length mix and share p50/p90/p99 and tokens/sec. For cost comparisons we'll include token-per-dollar estimates. Quick note: sequence length and batching are big cost/latency levers, so we'll match your estimated prompt sizes.
[03:06] Maya Chen: timeline wise Liam, can you run that benchmark next week and upload the spreadsheet so we can review before the next sync?
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: yep I'll run it on Tuesday and share by Thursday.
[03:17] Jon Martinez: okay timeline works for me as long as peering is done this week.
[03:22] Sara Lee: small question on encryption in transit, do you support mutual TLS for service endpoints?
[03:28] Maya Chen: yes mTLS is supported for Private deployments; for Hosted we use TLS + signed tokens, but we can enable mutual TLS for Dedicated if needed. We'll add that to the security doc.
[03:40] Priya Kapoor: also curious about KV cache persistence — we want to ensure some session affinity so cold starts aren't bad.
[03:46] Liam O'Connor: yes, the runtime supports KV caching and session affinity options; for the POC we usually enable prefix caching for repeated prompt patterns. Note the transcriber sometimes calls it 'KV cash' in the notes.
[03:58] Priya Kapoor: ha noted.
[04:02] Maya Chen: anything else on onboarding?
[04:05] Jon Martinez: I will finish the peering and test egress rules today; I'll send the firewall logs if there are failures.
[04:12] Sara Lee: I'll review the SOC2 artefacts once Maya shares and get back with any control gaps.
[04:17] Priya Kapoor: I'll drop the sample dataset and the service account details into the secure folder by Monday.
[04:23] Liam O'Connor: Great. For the benchmark, quick clarifying question on workload: do you want us to run chat-style prompts or single-turn generation traces?
[04:31] Priya Kapoor: mostly chat-style with context windows up to 1024 tokens, and a mix of short and medium replies, so please include both.
[04:38] Liam O'Connor: Got it, we'll include a mix: 0.5k, 1k sequence, and 2k in the spreadsheet where possible. We'll also try quantized variant to show cost savings tradeoffs.
[04:50] Maya Chen: one note on quantization — sometimes accuracy differences show up; we'll provide quality metrics (BLEU/QA accuracy) alongside latency.
[04:58] Priya Kapoor: okay that's important, please include a few reference prompts for eval.
[05:05] Liam O'Connor: will do.
[05:09] Maya Chen: recap - Redwood to run baseline benchmark (Liam), send exact CIDR/IP and iptables snippet (Liam), send KMS/SOC2 docs and retention info (Maya), Nexa to provide sample data and service account (Priya), Jon to finish VPC peering (Jon), Sara to confirm retention & controls (Sara).
[05:29] Priya Kapoor: that matches my notes. Any blockers on scheduling the canary?
[05:33] Maya Chen: no blockers on our side once we have benchmarks and peering. Targeting week of 7/20 for a small canary.
[05:41] Jon Martinez: ok we'll aim to have peering and firewall rules in by Monday so you can start tests.
[05:47] Sara Lee: I'll review security once docs arrive.
[05:50] Maya Chen: perfect, we'll follow up with an email and updated runbook link after this call. Thanks all.
[05:58] End of transcript (approx 30 minutes).
